newsitem.title: SYRIA: Arab air fleets seen needing to spend $20 billion.
newsitem.headline: Arab air fleets seen needing to spend $20 billion.

text.p: DAMASCUS, May 12 (reuter) - Arab countries need to spend $20 billion over the next 10 years to expand air fleets as demand for air transport picks up, a senior Arab aviation official said on Monday.
Khaled Slam, chairman of the executive committee of the Arab Air Carriers Organisation (AACO) told Reuters in an interview:
"According to studies, Arab states need to spend around $20 billion during the next 10 years to buy or lease planes to meet the increase in the air transportation."

Slam was in Damascus to attend an AACO meeting which opened on Monday. The Beirut-based AACO was established in 1965 as an offshoot of the Arab League to coordinate cooperation among Arab national air carriers.

Mohammed Habib Fakeh, deputy Middle East sales chief for European aircraft consortium Airbus, said Arab countries needed to buy or lease some 250 planes in the next decade. Most would be short- and medium-range aircraft.
"The Arab fleet now is over 350 planes and the number should reach 600 in the next 10 years," said Fakeh.
"According to studies we conducted, we expect demand to increase by five per cent per year in the next decade and this means the number of planes should increase to meet this increase," he said.
This was the estimated market open to all aircraft manufacturers, said Fakeh.

His participation at the meeting was at the invitation of AACO and was not aimed at concluding any commercial deals, he said. "We are here, as we used to be in the past, just to exchange views on issues concerning air transportation and to plan for the future." .

He said Airbus, which in December signed a contract to sell six A-320 planes to Syria, also had deals to sell or lease planes to the air carriers of Egypt, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Sudan and Yemen, along with Gulf Air.
"We have a good position in the Arab world at present," he said, adding it had enjoyed the biggest share among aircraft manufacturers recently.
